questions.question: Which of the following states does NOT share its border with Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Nagaland__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bangladesh is a country in South Asia that shares its border with India to the north, east, and west, Myanmar to the east, and the Bay of Bengal to the south.
 
• Tripura, Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Mizoram are the Indian state that shares their border with Bangladesh. 
 
• Dhaka, Rangpur, Khulna, Sylhet, Rajshahi, and Chittagong are the division of Bangladesh that are situated along the India Bangladesh Border.
 
• Nagaland does not share a border with Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Bangladesh became independent on **26 March 1971.**
 
• Bangladesh was proclaimed as an independent nation by Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and this led to Bangladesh Liberation War when a guerilla war ensued between Pakistan and Bangladesh liberation forces with Indian support.
 
• It launched a 10-day “golden jubilee” on March 17 with parades, fireworks, and tributes to independence hero Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

questions.question: Algae would generally NOT be found residing in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dry stone.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Algae **are a diverse group of aquatic organisms that have the** ability to conduct photosynthesis.**
 
• Algae are **prominent in bodies of water,** common in terrestrial environments, and are found in unusual environments, such as on snow and ice.
 
• Algae grow on wood in wet, dark conditions.
 
• Most of the soil algae, especially blue-green algae act as cementing agents in binding soil particles and thereby** prevent soil erosion.**
 
• In uncropped soil, soil algae** check the loss of nitrates through leaching and drainage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Algae can be classified on the basis of pigments present in them.
 
 
• **Chlorophyceae – green algae**
 
• **Phaeophyceae – brown algae**
 
• **Rhodophyceae – red algae**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Brown algae is a class of about 1,500 species of algae in the division Chromophyta, common in cold waters along continental coasts.
 
• Brown algae are an important source of algin, a colloidal gel used as a stabilizer in the baking and ice-cream industries.
 
• Red algae are red because of the presence of the pigment phycoerythrin; this pigment reflects red light and absorbs blue light.
 
• They are found in water bodies.
 
• Green algae have chloroplasts that contain chlorophyll a and b, giving them a bright green colour.
 
• The cell walls of green algae usually contain cellulose, and they store carbohydrates in the form of starch.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unit of energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kilowatt-hour.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Electrical energy: The energy that is derived from the flow of electric charge is called electrical energy.

 
 
• The SI unit of electrical energy is Joule.
 
 
 
• Kilowatt-hour:
 
 
• It is the unit of energy and is equal to the energy consumed in the circuit at the rate of 1 kilowatt for 1 hour.
 
• The commercial unit of electrical energy is a kilowatt-hour (kWh).
 
 
 
• Electric Power: The rate at which electrical energy is consumed in a circuit is called electric power.
 
 
• SI unit is the watt.
 
• One Kilowatt is equal to 1000 watts.
 
 

EXPLANATION__:

__
 
• The commercial unit of electrical energy is a kilowatt-hour (kWh). Therefore option 2 is correct.

 
• The commercial unit of electric energy is the kilowatt or the Board of Trade (B.O.T) unit.
 
• One kilowatt-hour is defined as the electric energy consumed by the appliance of 1 kilowatt in one hour and it is also called one unit of energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

1 kilowatt-hour = 1 kilowatt × 1 hours = 1000 watt × 3600 s

1 kWh = 3600000 joules = 3.6 × 106 J = 1 Unit of energy

questions.question: Inland streams which do NOT drain out into sea are generally found in which state of India?

• Rivers Luni, Ghaggar, Rupnarain, Medha, etc have inland drainage.

questions.question: Who addressed the Congress as President in 1887 thus - "This Congress is composed of the representatives, not of any one class or community of India, but of all the different communities of India"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Badruddin Tyabji.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Badruddin Tyabji: 

 
 
• He was an Indian political activist during British Raj.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He served as the third President of the Indian National Congress from 1887 to 1888.
 
• He addressed the Congress as President held at **Madras** in 1887.
 
• **He said,** "This Congress is composed of the representatives, not of any one class or community of India, but of all the different communities of India".
 
• He became a Barrister in April 1867.
 
• He was the first Indian to be admitted to the High Court of Bombay as a barrister.
 
• In 1902, he became the first Indian to serve as Chief Justice in Bombay.
 
• The first Muslim politician to build a secular political awareness was Badruddin Tyabji.
 
• The 'Triumvirate' ('The Three Stars') of Bombay's public life were Badruddin Tyabji, Pherozeshah Mehta, and Kashinath Telang.
 
 

 [IMAGE: http://photos.geni.com/p12/9b/42/35/9f/53444838914677fe/badruddin_tyabji_2_original.jpg] 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Surendranath Banerjee**

 
 
• He founded a nationalist organization called the Indian National Association.
 
• Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose were its main organisers.
 
• Surendranath Banerjee convened an all-India conference at Kolkata from 25 to 27 December 1885.
 
• Two sessions of the conference were held in 1883 and 1885.
 
• He cleared the Indian Civil Service competitive examination in 1869 but was barred owing to a claim he had misrepresented his age. 
 
• He wrote the book** "****A Nation in Making"**.
 
 
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**
 
 
• He led the **Congress Banaras session in 1905.**​
 
• He was a member of the Imperial Legislative Council.
 
• He was popularly famous as a great champion of compulsory primary education for the first time in India.
 
• He publicly demanded the introduction of “Compulsory Primary Education” in India. 
 
• He was also the founder of the **Servants of India Society.**
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**
 
 
• Dadabhai Naroji presided over Congress three times.
 
• He was the Congress president during the 1886, 1893, and 1906 sessions. 
 
• He had also been the founder-editor of the journal Rast Goftar in Bombay in 1851.
 
• He founded the London Zoroastrian Association in 1861.
 
• He was also a founding member of the East India Association and London Indian Society.
 
• He was an economist and proponent of the drain theory, building up a detailed economic critique of British imperialism in India.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is NOT observed on a full moon day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eid-al-Fitr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eid-Ul-Fitr**

 
 
• **Eid-Ul-Fitr **marks the end of the holy month of **Ramadan** and is celebrated by the Muslim community across the globe.
 
• **It starts the day after the observation of the crescent moon, which usually occurs one night after the new moon**.
 
• Eid-Ul-Fitr, also known as** Meethi Eid, marks the end of Roza (fast),** which is observed during the whole month of Ramadan.
 
• On Eid-Ul-Fitr, Muslims thank Allah for offering them health and resistance during Ramadan.
 
• This festival is observed on the first day of **Shawwal** - the month that comes after Ramadan in the Hijri calendar.
 
• Additionally, the beginning of any lunar Hijri month varies according to the new moon sighting by religious authorities.
 
• And since Eid Ul-Fitr also marks the first day of Shawwal month, it is celebrated on different days across regions.
 
• Muslims also observe Eid-Ul-Adha, which follows soon after Eid Ul-Fitr.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shab-e-Barat**

 
 
• Shab-e-Barat a major celebration for the Muslim community is also known as the night of fortune and forgiveness. 
 
• Shab e-Barat takes place on the** full moon** and the date of the public holiday in Bangladesh
 
 
 
• **Buddha Jayanti**
 
 
• According to Buddhist legends, Buddha was born as Prince Siddhartha Gautama on the Baisakh full moon day in 563 BC at Lumbini in Nepal.
 
• His birth anniversary is also known as Vaisakhi Buddha Purnima or Vesak.
 
• The **full moon day, **Buddha Purnima is the most sacred day for Buddhists.
 
 
 
• **Rakshabandhan**
 
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, the holy festival of Raksha Bandhan is celebrated on the** full moon **day of Shukla Paksha of Shravan month.
 
• The holy festival of Rakshabandhan is a symbol of the love of brother and sister.

questions.question: A ______ performance begins with the kelikottu, calling the audience to attention followed by the todayam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kathakali

 
 
• Kathakali derives its name from the words ‘Katha’ meaning story, and ‘Kali’ meaning drama.
 
• It is a wonderful combination of music, dance, and drama.
 
• It is presented in the temple precincts after dusk falls.
 
• A **Kathakali **performance is heralded by the Kelikottu or the beating of drums to the accompaniment of the Chengila (gong).
 
• It is over 300 years old. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Kathakali

 
 
• Kathakali dance originated in** Kerala.**
 
• It is one of the **eight classical dances in India **recognised bySangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• It is closely related to Koodiyattam (Sanskrit drama tradition) and other ancient martial arts performances also. 
 
• Most of the Kathakali recitals are a grand representation of the eternal conflict between good and evil.
 
• It draws its themes from the stories narrated in the epics and the Puranas.
 
 
• It is also called the ‘ballad of the east
 
 
 
• The Indigenous Music of Kerala 'Sopana Sangeetham ' is used in Kathakali.
 
• The instruments used in the Kathakali are Chenda (a type of drum), Madhalam (a long cylindrical drum), Chengila ( gong), and Ilathalam (an instrument similar to a cymbal). Sometimes Idakka (a type of small drum) is also used. 
 
• Gestures are perhaps the crown jewel of the entire dance drama.
 
• Kathakali is remarkable in the representation of the rasas through movements of the eye and eyebrows, through which the story is conveyed.
 
• **Nine important facial expressions called ‘Navarasas**’ are taught to convey** different emotions.**

questions.question:
Which of the given statements is/are correct?

(a) The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is appointed by the President of India.

(b) The CAG shall only be removed from office in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

(c) The CAG shall not be eligible for further office either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State after he/she has ceased to hold his/her office.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(a), (b) and (c).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Chapter 5 of Part 5 of the Constitution describes the Comptroller and Auditor General.
 
• After independence, Article 148 of the Indian Constitution provided for the appointment of a Comptroller and Auditor General by the President of India. **(hence A is correct)**
 
• Article 148-151 deals with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
 
• He will be removed in the same way that a Supreme Court judge is removed. (hence B is correct)​
 
 
• ​Process: Based on the resolution passed by a special majority of both houses.
 
• Proven malpractice and incapability
 
 
 
• Tenure: 6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
 
• He submits his resignation to President.
 
• **Not eligible for re-appointment. (Hence statement (a), (b) and (c) are correct)**

questions.question: The 42ⁿd Amendment of the Constitution of India was passed in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 42nd Amendment of the Constitution of India: **

 
 
• The 42nd Amendment of the Constitution of India was **enacted **in the year 1976.
 
• It is officially known as the** Constitution Act, 1976.**
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency by the Indian National Congress Head Indira Gandhi.
 
• It is considered the **most controversial Constitutional Amendment** in Indian history.
 
• It is often called a **"mini-Constitution"** or the **"Constitution of Indira".**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Some Important Provisions of the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976

 
 
• Added three new words** socialists, secular, and integrity** in the Preamble.
 
• Added Fundamental Duties by the citizens** (new part IV A).**
 
• Made the President bound by the advice of the cabinet.
 
• Provided administrative tribunals and tribunals for other matters (Added Part XIV A).
 
• Added three new DPSPs i.e. equal justice and free legal aid, participation of workers in the management of industries, and protection of the environment, forest, and wildlife.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?

A: Kuttanad is in the state of Karnataka.

B: Kuttanad Agriculture System favours rice cultivation below sea level.

C: Kuttanad is a Ramsar site and a reputed destination for water tourism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Only A__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuttanad Wetland Agriculture System (KWAS)**

 
 
• **Kuttanad is a region in Kerala** that has many interesting aspects emanating from its culture, evolution, agricultural practices, and many more. ***Hence statement A is incorrect***.
 
• It is a land where backwaters and canals make their presence felt more than any other region in Kerala.
 
• In **2002**, it was included in the **list of wetlands of international importance**, as defined by the **Ramsar Convention. ***Hence statement C is correct.*
 
• **KWAS is unique, as it is the only system in India that favors rice cultivation below sea level on the land**. *Hence statement B is correct*
 
• It is created by draining delta swamps in brackish waters.
 
• The Kuttanad system is a complex mosaic of fragmented agricultural landscapes divided into three structures, i.e. wetlands used for paddy activities and fish catching, garden lands used for coconut, tubers, and food crops plantation, and water areas used for inland fishing and shells.
 
• Its predominant rice cultivation has earned Kuttanad the sobriquet - The rice bowl of Kerala.
 
• Here, annually three crops are grown.
 
• In earlier days when rice farming started gaining popularity in Kuttanad, large parts of Vembanad Lake were reclaimed by local farmers for rice cultivation.

questions.question: What was the result of the Test series (February-March 2021) between India and England Men's cricket team?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India won 3-1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **England tour of India (February-March 2021)**__

 __
 
• A total of **4 test**,** 5 T20I** and **3 ODI** was held from **5th February **to **28th March 2021** in** India**.
 
• India won the Test series **3-1**, T20I series** 3-2** and ODI series** 2-1**.
 
• **R Ashwin** was given the** man of the series** for this** Test series**.
 
• Captain **Virat Kohli **was given the** man of the series** for this **T20I series**.
 
• **Jonny Bairstow** was given the** man of the series** for this **ODI series**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** ICC__**

 __
 
• The **International Cricket Council **(ICC), the international governing body of Cricket founded in **1909 **by representatives from **England**,** Australia**, and** South Africa**.
 
• It was initially known as the** Imperial Cricket Conference**.
 
• In **1965**, it was renamed as **International Cricket Conference**.
 
• it was renamed the** International Cricket Council **(ICC) in **1989**.
 
• Headquarters of ICC -** Dubai**, **UAE**
 
• Motto - **Cricket for good**
 
• Chairman -** Greg Barclay**
 
 
 
• **BCCI**__
 
 
• The full form of the BCCI is the **Board of Control for Cricket in India**.
 
• The board was formed in **December 1928** as a society, registered under the **Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act**.
 
• BCCI is **an autonomous body** and does not review any grants or funding from the Sports Ministry of India.
 
• Present chairman of BCCI is** Sourav Ganguly**.
 
• The present secretary of BCCI is **Jay Shah**.
 
• The current President of **Asian Cricket Council **is **Jay Shah**.
